Maya (finance): FYI — I pulled the February GCP Marketplace payout and there's a negative adjustment of about $18,321 compared to our internal invoices. Anyone seen a delta like this before?

Sophie (reconciliations): Oof. Can you paste the statement lines? Is it labeled as 'reseller adjustment' or something else?

Maya (finance): Pasted the relevant rows below. The marketplace payout shows a "NET_ADJ" line for invoice 8a3f-... and a -18,321.00 amount. Our invoice capture has the full amount.

```
Statement excerpt:
OrderID: ORD-2026-02-1179
Subscription: sub-9c2b
Invoice: 8a3f-2026-02
Gross: 412,345.00
ResellerFee: -24,740.00
NET_ADJ: -18,321.00
NetPayout: 369,284.00
```

Arjun (cloudops): Quick thought — did we change any reseller mapping for committed CPU/GPU SKUs last month? GCP sometimes reclassifies committed use discounts or commitment refunds and shows them as adjustments on the marketplace side.

Liam (billing): We didn't change mapping intentionally, but there was a cleanup script that ended up reassigning a few legacy commit SKUs to the partner account on Feb 10. That could surface as a retrospective adjustment.

Sophie (reconciliations): If it's a reclassification/refund flow, GCP usually includes a reference to the original invoice or commit ID in the adjustment detail. Can you export the full CSV (line_item_id + referencing_invoice) and paste the rows?

Maya (finance): Uploading CSV snippet: 
```
line_item_id,description,ref_invoice,amount
li-00123,Compute Engine (n1-highmem) commit correction,8a3f-2026-01,-9,432.00
li-00456,Marketplace reseller fee correction,, -8,889.00
li-00789,Tax/commodity adj,8a3f-2026-01,-0.00
```

Arjun (cloudops): The li-00123 referencing 8a3f-2026-01 looks like a retroactive adjustment to a committed GPU/CPU reservation we cancelled for a cluster in us-west1. We had that node pool decommed on Jan 22 when we moved workloads to dedicated hosts. If the partner account was still tied to that subscription, marketplace would issue an adj.

Liam (billing): That matches our internal change log — I see a deprovision request for the Dedicated pool (commit-id cmt-44b) on Jan 22. But the internal invoice shows a credit applied to the commit, not a marketplace negative payout. So it's a mismatch in where the credit landed.

Sophie (reconciliations): Action items: 1) Maya — open a Partner Support case with GCP asking for adjustment mappings for OrderID ORD-2026-02-1179 and reference li-00123 & li-00456. Ask them to provide original invoice refs for each adj. 2) Arjun — confirm whether commit cmt-44b was transferred to partner billing or closed on our side. 3) Liam — run a reconciliation of our ledger vs marketplace export and flag any entries with missing ref_invoice.

Maya (finance): I'll open the case now and add the CSV snapshot. Draft: "Partner payout includes NET_ADJ -18,321. Please provide detailed mapping to original invoices/commit IDs for Order ORD-2026-02-1179, specifically line items li-00123 and li-00456." Anything to add?

Arjun (cloudops): Include the cluster name (dedicated-prod-usw1) and the deprovision timestamp (2026-01-22T03:12:00Z). Also ask if marketplace ever bills repayments/chargebacks for partner-resold commitments separately from our invoice feed.

Liam (billing): Request the partner settlement report for the payout cycle as a CSV. Sometimes the UI glues entries but the settlement CSV has internal notes (commit transfer id).

GCP Marketplace Bot: Note: Support cases typically respond in 2-5 business days for partner payout disputes. If you include purchase and settlement IDs it speeds triage.

Sophie (reconciliations): In parallel, I'll run a tag-based query to see if any other decommissions touched partner-owned SKUs in Jan-Feb. If we find more, this might be a systemic mapping bug.

Maya (finance): Case created: #GP-83412 by Maya. I've attached CSV and requested settlement CSV + mapping. ETA 3 business days. I'll post updates here.

Liam (billing): I've started the ledger diff and will post a short table in ~2 hours. If it's a mapping issue, we should consider a short-term accrual adjustment so MRR numbers don't swing.

Arjun (cloudops): Also checking network/region note — dedicated-prod-usw1 had some IP migration on Jan 21 that touched billing tags. Might explain why GCP attributed the commit to partner. I'll trace tag changes.

Sophie (reconciliations): Good catch. Tag drift is a frequent root cause. If partner account gets the tag, marketplace assumes resale path.

Maya (finance): Thanks all. For now tracking as P0 because it's material to Feb payout. Will update when GCP replies. :thumbsup:

Liam (billing): :thumbsup:

Arjun (cloudops): Will ping infra team for the tag fix if we see drift.

Sophie (reconciliations): If GCP confirms it's their side, we'll request a corrected settlement and a reissued payout. If it's on our tagging, we need a retro allocation so marketplace matches our invoices.

Maya (finance): Closing loop — will post case updates and a reconciliation summary once we have their response.
